steps.message:
The edit itself is one line (`config.js:3`, `SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES: 30` → `480`), but it's a session-lifetime change, so it has a consequence beyond the line: a stolen or abandoned session token stays valid for 8 hours instead of 30 — a 16× wider window for session hijacking on shared or unattended machines, and 16× longer before a revoked/compromised account is actually logged out. `server.js:2` confirms this value is the sole expiry control here; there's no idle-timeout or re-auth step to limit the blast radius.

That may well be exactly what you want (long-running internal tool, dev convenience). I just want your explicit go-ahead before changing it.

options.description: Set the absolute timeout to 8 hours but also add a shorter idle expiry, so unattended sessions still die quickly. This is a design change, not a one-liner.
